permutationLabel: High-voltage electrical, small visible TBSA, myoglobinuria
summary: 30-year-old lineman, 75 kg, 11 kV contact 1 h ago with brief loss of consciousness: charred entry wound right hand, exit wound left foot, 4 % visible TBSA; tense right forearm; dark brown urine, CK 18,000, K 5.6.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Electrical injury at work, high voltage
inputs.hpi: Power-line worker, contact with an 11 kV line 1 hour ago. Thrown from the ladder, knocked out briefly. Burn on the right hand and left foot. Passing dark brown urine.

exam.general: GCS 15. HR 112, BP 132/80, RR 20, SpO2 98%. Weight 75 kg.
exam.skin: Charred full-thickness entry wound on the right palm (1.5%) and exit wound on the left sole (1%), with surrounding partial-thickness burns — 4% visible TBSA. Right forearm tense and swollen, pain on passive finger extension.

labs.name: Urine dipstick
labs.resultText: Dark brown urine, blood +++, microscopy no red cells (myoglobinuria)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: High-voltage electrical injury with myoglobinuria and forearm compartment syndrome risk
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: High-voltage (11 kV) electrical injury: visible TBSA 4% underestimates deep muscle injury; myoglobinuria, CK 18,000, K 5.6; tense forearm. ECG and cardiac monitoring, IV fluids to urine output 1–1.5 mL/kg/h until the urine clears, fasciotomy assessment, burns centre.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 3 of ios.bayes: 1. Acute Kidney Injury | 2. Medication Side Effect / Adverse Drug Reaction | 3. Anxiety Disorder | 4. Preventive / Screening Visit | 5. Hypertensive Emergency

mustInclude.note: Fluids are driven by pigmented urine, not by the visible TBSA.

mustExclude.note: Small visible TBSA must not lead to oral fluids in high-voltage injury with myoglobinuria.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — thermal injuries
guideline.section: Chapter 9: stop the burning process; early airway control for inhalation injury (hoarseness, stridor, carbonaceous sputum, singed facial hair, enclosed-space fire); 100% oxygen and carboxyhaemoglobin for suspected CO; TBSA by rule of nines (adults) or Lund–Browder (children); fluid resuscitation titrated to urine output (adult 0.5 mL/kg/h, child ≤30 kg 1 mL/kg/h, high-voltage electrical injury with pigmented urine 1–1.5 mL/kg/h); children also need maintenance glucose-containing fluid; escharotomy for circumferential full-thickness burns; chemical burns — remove agent and irrigate with copious water; electrical — ECG and cardiac monitoring, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 9. (Lund–Browder chart: Lund CC, Browder NC. The estimation of areas of burns. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1944;79:352–8.)

guideline.name: American Burn Association — burn centre referral criteria
guideline.section: Refer: partial-thickness burns >10% TBSA; burns involving face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum or major joints; full-thickness burns in any age group; electrical burns (including lightning); chemical burns; inhalation injury; burns with pre-existing medical disorders or concomitant trauma; burned children in hospitals without qualified personnel; patients needing special social or rehabilitative support (including suspected abuse). (2022 ABA update to be checked)
guideline.citation: American Burn Association / American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Guidelines for the operation of burn centers — burn center referral criteria. In: Resources for Optimal Care of the Injured Patient. Chicago: ACS; 2006.

guideline.name: National Network for Burn Care (British Burn Association) — National Burn Care Referral Guidance
guideline.section: Referral to a specialised burn service by size (children and adults, partial thickness or more), all full-thickness and circumferential burns, special areas (face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum, major joints), chemical, electrical, friction and cold injuries, inhalation injury, suspected non-accidental injury, and burns not healed in 2 weeks (thresholds to be checked against the source)
guideline.citation: National Network for Burn Care. National Burn Care Referral Guidance. Version 1. London: NNBC; 2012.

rationale: Permutation: high-voltage electrical injury. The visible TBSA (4 %) is well below the fluid threshold, but deep muscle injury with myoglobinuria needs IV fluids to a higher urine-output target, ECG monitoring and compartment assessment. This is the case where a TBSA-driven fluid rule is dangerous.
